howToRegenerate: node scripts/check-content.mjs --print-baseline  (prints this shape; it never writes it)
ruleOfExit: A pair leaves this file when the copy is deleted or a ruling settles it. It is NOT kept with status 'resolved': a signature in this file is an exemption, so keeping a closed pair would let the same duplicate ship again without going red. The pairs closed by S018/D262 and by D273 are listed in `resolved` below for provenance only.
signatureNote: A signature has its date stamps removed before anything else (DATE_STAMP in scripts/check-content.mjs). `npm run events:harvest` rewrites "Copied from the club's own calendar on <date>" each time the feed is read, and a signature that carries the stamp's date is an exemption with an expiry: @measured 2026-11-13 by this gate, one harvest moved the stamp from Nov 6 to Nov 13 and made all 3 baseline rows stale — three FAILs for sentences nobody edited. The date the page prints is data, not the shape of the sentence.

resolved.how: the band's line deleted; the hero keeps the one statement of where dates and discussion live

resolved.pair: hero syllabus line <> band's homework line
resolved.how: the band's homework line deleted; the hero's syllabus sentence now carries the chat statement too

resolved.pair: hero threads signpost <> 'What we take up' opener
resolved.how: the hero signpost became the syllabus line; the section opener kept its sourcing clause, because check:content refuses an unsourced list (D92)

resolved.pair: 'Details and sign-up on Meetup' on row A <> 'Details and sign-up on Meetup' on row B
resolved.how: the row label became a per-platform name ('Sign up on Meetup', 'Sign up on Discord'), so sibling rows no longer print the same sentence; the baseline row was deleted rather than kept as an exemption

scores: content words only; sentences split on terminal punctuation only. A pair is a pair when it shares >=3 content words and (Jaccard >= 0.45 or overlap >= 0.5). Overlap is shared words over the SHORTER sentence, because a paraphrase of a long sentence scores low on Jaccard alone.

statusMeaning.open: the repeat is real and unruled: the gate stays green on it; deleting one side or taking a ruling is the exit
statusMeaning.deliberate: the repeat is the point of the surface - a source line or a ruling says so, in why
statusMeaning.template: identical row furniture on sibling rows: one string rendered twice. Coupling, not duplication - if one row changes, both must

rowFurniture.what: Strings printed in more than one schedule row (`<li data-surface="row">`). The gate computes them from the artifact every run and reports them; it never reads this list, so this is provenance, not an exemption. A row and a section paragraph printing the same sentence still FAILS, and two rows that paraphrase each other still FAILS - the exemption is only for the identical string in two rows (proven by `check:content:selftest`, plants `row-furniture-not-a-duplicate`, `row-sentence-in-a-section-paragraph`, `rows-that-paraphrase`).
rowFurniture.ruledBy: D273 (row furniture is coupling, not duplication)

pairs.signature: copied from the club's own calendar <> the date above is copied from the club's own calendar and it links to the page where you sign up
pairs.ruled: D273 (the band lede was reworded to say what the date links to)
pairs.surfaces: section:When We Meet (homepage next-date band lede) <> section:MPLS Math Club Social (the date stamp inside the preview card)
pairs.why: Both surfaces draw a date from the same snapshot and each states its provenance where the date is painted - the rule the earlier band/row pair was accepted for. The band speaks for the page, the stamp speaks for one date, so a reader who sees only the card still knows where its date came from. Accepted: the repeat is the source line, not decorative copy. It becomes a defect only if one of the two stops carrying a date or a source.

pairs.signature: copied from the club's own calendar <> the club's list of members is its meetup group page last the list is not the room
pairs.surfaces: section:MPLS Math Club Social (the date stamp on the preview card) <> section:How it works (the membership sentence)
pairs.why: Scored on shared dated-source vocabulary (club, calendar, meetup, page), not on a repeated sentence: overlap reaches 0.5 only because the shorter string is four words. Recorded so the pair stays visible; the exit is a ruling or a stamp that carries its date in different words.

pairs.why: The same provenance rule on the schedule page: the page lede and the list stamp each say where the dates came from. D218 keeps the stamp once for the list rather than once per row.
